'''Vladimir Alekseevich Belinski''' (last name is also spelled '''Belinsky''', {{langx|ru|Владимир Алексеевич Белинский}}; born 26 March 1941)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.icra.it/People/Belinski.htm|title=Vladimir Belinski|publisher=International Center for Relativistic Astrophysics}}</ref> is a Russian and [[Italy|Italian]] theoretical physicist involved in research in [[cosmology]] and [[general relativity]]. He worked at [[Landau Institute for Theoretical Physics]] from 1968 to 1989 and got his [[Habilitation]] ([[Doctor of Sciences]]) degree at this Institute in 1980.<ref>{{cite web|title=Диссертации, подготовленные или защищенные в ИТФ им. Л.Д. Ландау|url=http://itp.ac.ru/ru/dissertation-council/thesis/}}</ref> As of 2016, he holds the permanent professor position at [[International Network of the Centers for Relativistic Astrophysics]] (ICRANet), Italy.

Belinski contributed to the editing of some chapters in [[Lev Landau|Landau]] and [[Evgeny Lifshitz|Lifshitz]]'s [[Course of Theoretical Physics|course of theoretical physics]] for volume 2. One of his most notable scientific contributions is [[BKL conjecture]] (Belinski—[[Khalatnikov]]—[[Evgeny Lifshitz|Lifshitz]] conjecture) on the behavior of generic solutions of [[Einstein field equations]] near a [[cosmological singularity]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Belinski|first1=V.|last2=Khalatnikov|first2=I.|last3=Lifshitz|first3=E.|title=Oscillatory Approach to a Singular Point in the Relativistic Cosmology|journal=Adv. Phys.|date=1970|volume=19|issue=80|page=525|doi=10.1080/00018737000101171|bibcode=1970AdPhy..19..525B}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Belinski|first1=V.|last2=Khalatnikov|first2=I.|last3=Lifshitz|first3=E.|title=A general solution of the Einstein equations with a time singularity|journal=Adv. Phys.|date=1982|volume=31|issue=6|page=639|bibcode=1982AdPhy..31..639B|doi=10.1080/00018738200101428}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Belinski|first1=V.|title=On the cosmological singularity|journal=International Journal of Modern Physics D|date=2014|volume=23|issue=7|pages=1430016–215|arxiv=1404.3864|bibcode=2014IJMPD..2330016B|doi=10.1142/S021827181430016X}}</ref> He co-invented the [[Belinski-Zakharov transform]] in 1978 showing that black holes are a special example of gravitational solitons.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Belinski|first1=Vladimir A.|last2=Verdaguer|first2=Enric|title=Gravitational Solitons|publisher= [[Cambridge University Press]]|year= 2001|isbn= 978-0-521-80586-5}}</ref> Another his notable result (obtained in 1985—1987 together with L. Grischuk, [[Khalatnikov|I. Khalatnikov]] and [[Zeldovich|Ya. Zeldovich]]) is discovery of the "Inflationary Attractor". This is the unique solution of the gravitational equations with [[massive scalar field]] which solution has maximal degree of [[inflation]] and attract the majority of all other solutions forcing them to have the prolonged inflationary stages.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Belinski|first1=V.|last2=Grishchuk|first2=L.|last3=Khalatnikov|first3=I.|last4=Zeldovich|first4=Y.|title=Inflationary Stages in Cosmological Models with a Scalar Field|journal=Phys. Lett. B|date=1985|volume=155|issue=4|page=232|doi=10.1016/0370-2693(85)90644-6|bibcode=1985PhLB..155..232B}}<br/>{{cite journal|last1=Belinski|first1=V.|last2=Grishchuk|first2=L.|last3=Khalatnikov|first3=I.|last4=Zeldovich|first4=Y.|title=Inflationary Stages in Cosmological Models with a Scalar Field|journal=Sov. Phys. JETP|date=1985|volume=62|page=195|bibcode=1985ZhETF..89..346B}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Belinski|first1=V.|last2=Khalatnikov|first2=I.|title=On the generality of inflationary solutions in cosmological models with a scalar field|journal=Sov. Phys. JETP|date=1987|volume=66|page=441|bibcode=1987ZhETF..93..784B}}</ref>

==Awards==
* [[Landau Prize]] of the Russian Academy of Sciences (1974) "For set of works on singularities in Relativistic Cosmology"
* [http://www.icra.it/mg/mg13/mg13_awards.pdf Marcel Grossmann Award] (2012) "For the discovery of a general solution of the Einstein equations with a cosmological singularity of an oscillatory chaotic character known as the [[BKL singularity]]"
